source.how: Both Map 5.1 sheets are ArcGIS Pro GeoPDFs: the Areas_of_Special_Concern frame carries a /VP viewport with its corner coordinates (NAD83 HARN geographic, projected to EPSG:2913); a page-to-ground affine was fitted to them (residual 0.57 ft Raleigh Hills, 0.09 ft Bull Mountain) and the pink-filled ASC outlines (RGB 1, 0.745, 0.745) were read out of the page as vector paths. Each outline took the red Arial-Bold letter or numeral within 50 ft of it; Raleigh Hills prints no letter near some outlines, and an outline more than 600 ft from every letter is 'unlabelled'. A lot is in an ASC when at least 90 percent of it lies inside the outline, and the lots an outline cuts (more than 10 percent inside) are carried too, whole. This file holds, whole, the residential lots (R-5 to R-25+) on which a plan rule binds a pod that the screen cannot measure: Raleigh Hills ASC S and T lots whose boundary runs at least 15 ft within 40 ft of the Mayo Street or Florence Lane centreline or 60 ft of Taylors Ferry Road's (the access-point caps bind only those streets); every ASC M lot (one access point on Raab Road for the whole ASC; ASC I's bar on permanent highway access reaches no residential lot); the residential lots inside the commercial-strip ASCs (E, H, K, L and the unlettered outlines within 600 ft of those letters) that abut Canyon Road, Beaverton - Hillsdale Highway, Scholls Ferry Road or Oleson Road (Type 1 landscape buffer, CDC 411 not stored); the ASC U lot (Case #74-96C conditions); every lot of an unlettered outline more than 600 ft from any letter (two outlines: at Walker Road and Highway 217, ASC C by the text, and one lot west of SW 103rd Avenue); the lots Map 8.1 shades in its one drawn pedestrian connectivity area (magenta fill RGB 1, 0.451, 0.875, read as vector paths; more than 10 percent of the lot) and, for area 3, which no map draws, every lot meeting a 40 ft buffer of the straight line between the nearest points of the Dogwood Lane and Raleighwood Way centrelines and of Dogwood Lane and Sharon Lane (a judgement trace: the plan places the trail in words only; area 1's Laurel Street already meets Laurelwood Avenue and Maple Drive's gap crosses no lot); Bull Mountain ASC 1, every lot inside or cut (the easterly portion is not drawn, so the traffic-study bar is held on all of it, with the three-access-point cap); the residential lot fronting Pacific Highway (within 60 ft, 15 ft of boundary); and the two parcels Bull Mountain's Map 8.1 shades for the Baker Lane / Sunrise Lane area. Bull Mountain's Map 8.1 is a raster: page 11 was rendered at 432 dpi, magenta pixels (R>220, 70<G<160, B>180) inside the main frame were placed by the frame's affine (4.6 ft a pixel), and a lot is shaded when they cover more than 10 percent of it (the two cover 0.88 and 0.84).
